messages:
Sam Carter: Customer 'Meridian Health' reports they get a 403 when switching projects in the Console after an IDP Conditional Access prompt. Happens right after MFA/CA policy triggers and user completes reauth in Okta/Azure. They say UI shows 'Action blocked' and no hint to re-login.
Priya Nair: Can you paste the user's browser console / network error? is it the iframe auth callback failing or our API rejecting the session?
Sam Carter: Customer pasted this snippet from the Console network panel: 
```
POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/sessions/validate 403
Response: {"error":"forbidden","reason":"membership_not_found"}
```
They also included a SAML relay-state trace (redacted) showing a successful auth but group claims shorter than before.
Liam O'Connor: membership_not_found usually means the id claim we trust for project membership didn't match any project-binding. Could be group claim truncated by CA or by a token-size policy. Do we have an audit log for the user's last successful SCIM sync?
Sam Carter: Support agent ran a quick check — user id retained in org but project membership removed at 2024-11-05T16:40:12Z. SCIM logs show a partial group list in the last push. Customer says their IDP enforced a Conditional Access session refresh which may have re-emitted a smaller claim set.
Jorge Alvarez: @idp-bot can you pull the last inbound SAML assertion we stored for this user (assertion id: XXXX-REDACTED) and show the groups vs the one at previous login?
idp-bot: Stored assertion snapshot pulled. Current assertion group claim length = 3. Previous assertion group claim length = 12. Several project groups missing (project-analytics, project-ops).
Priya Nair: Ok so root cause seems to be: CA policy forced a fresh auth that resulted in different claim emission (IdP filtered groups during CA reauth). Our session validation compares the claim->project bindings and concluded the user no longer has membership => API returns 403 on project-scoped actions.
Liam O'Connor: Short-term workaround: ask customer to re-add the user to the missing groups in their IdP (or run a SCIM resync) so the next assertion contains proper group membership. Also a Console UX workaround: sign out and sign back in (full log-out, not just page refresh) — that will create a fresh session and re-evaluate claims.
Sam Carter: Customer tried sign-out/sign-in and still got 403. Support-agent: can you confirm they cleared cookies + did a full sign-out? Many idp CA flows reuse existing session unless cleared.
support-agent: Confirmed they cleared cookies, full sign out, then sign-in. Still 403. After manual SCIM resync from customer Okta, membership re-propagated and user regained project access. Customer reports resolved. :white_check_mark:
Priya Nair: Action items: 1) Add diagnostic message in Console UI on 403 for project-switch that suggests re-auth or group-resync (e.g., 'Your IdP claims no longer include this project. Try signing out or contact your IdP admin.'); 2) Add extra logging on session validation failure to surface which claim was expected vs present (non-PII) so support can triage quicker; 3) Follow up with integrations/IDP team to consider caching previous group snapshot during short window to avoid immediate 403 on CA reauth (needs security review).
Liam O'Connor: For triage we need the following from customer if it recurs: - exact timestamp of the 403, - user principal (email), - SAML assertion id (or OAuth id_token kid), - SCIM delta logs around that time. Also collect browser user-agent to rule out size/trimming middleware.
Jorge Alvarez: Noted. I'll create a quick KB snippet for support with the step-by-step repro and the Okta/Azure CA caveats. Will link to it in the ticket.
Sam Carter: Ticket updated, escalated to idp-infra for follow-up on claim truncation possibilities. Customer is happy for now. Closing loop: consider adding a health check or alert when SCIM pushes start reporting falling group counts (>50% drop) for any heavy-org. :lock::warning:
